content.title: What Analysts Think Is Resetting The Story For Clorox (CLX)
content.summary: The latest update on Clorox trims the modelled fair value estimate slightly, from US$124.59 to US$122.41, as analysts factor in softer revenue growth assumptions of 1.39% versus 1.43% previously. This small adjustment reflects a tug of war between cautious views, tied to weaker Q1 results and a lower end EPS outlook, and more constructive voices who see reset expectations and clustered targets in the low to mid US$120s as a sign that the story is being recalibrated rather than abandoned. content.title: These Five Stocks Had Their Worst Year in Decades
content.summary: Pressures including U.S. tariffs, AI-related disruption and more pummeled five companies in 2025 to the point that they had their worst annual performance in at least 20 years, according to Dow Jones Market Data.  Drinks-maker Constellation Brands’ 37% drop puts it on pace for its worst loss since 1987.  Brown & Brown’s 22% tumble is on track to be the insurer’s toughest year since 1990.

content.title: Clorox’s 5% Yield Looks Solid but One Metric Deserves Attention
content.summary: Clorox (NYSE:CLX) operates household brands including Clorox bleach, Glad trash bags, Burt’s Bees, Hidden Valley, and Fresh Step cat litter. The company pays an annual dividend of $4.92 per share, yielding just under 5%. That yield looks attractive, but it’s elevated because the stock has collapsed 37% over the past year.
